## What it is

Frigate is a network video recorder (NVR) for IP cameras with local, real-time object detection: it records the cameras' RTSP streams, detects people, cars and animals on the box, and offers a web UI for live view, review and history ([blakeblackshear/frigate](https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate)). It is the recorder behind the OneMind video wall (plan row C2).

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API for the repository; Market class **L1**). Checked for #245:

- The image is upstream's standard multi-arch image, unchanged. Its built-in detection models come from [google-coral/test_data](https://github.com/google-coral/test_data) (Apache-2.0) and the [OpenVINO Open Model Zoo](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/open_model_zoo) (Apache-2.0, an SSDLite model converted from the TensorFlow model zoo), plus Google's YAMNet audio model (`docker/main/Dockerfile`). No model is downloaded at run time.
- **Frigate+** (paid models and training at `api.frigate.video`) is never configured: it only runs when an API key is set, and this app sets none.
- The hardware-specific images (`-tensorrt`, `-rocm`, `-rk`, `-synaptics`, `-tensorrt-jp6`) are not used: they are separate images the scan gate does not cover here.
- **Brand:** the Frigate name and logo are trademarks outside the MIT licence (`docs/static/img/branding/LICENSE.md` upstream). The Market shows a neutral initials icon; the unmodified UI shows its own logo when run, which that notice allows.

## How it runs here

- **Recordings stay on the box.** Video lives on `frigate-media`, a volume on this machine's own disk (the cluster default class, no network share). Recordings, snapshots, previews and exports are excluded from every backup, local or off-site (`spec.backup.exclude`); the backup keeps only `frigate-config` (config, users, the event database, copied online as SQLite). Only the signed-in port 8971 is exposed.
- **No outbound calls by Frigate itself.** The seeded config turns off the GitHub version check (`telemetry.version_check: false`) and MQTT, sets no Frigate+ key and no generative AI, and the container sets `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1` (frigate/network_requirements.md, "Running Frigate Offline"). Features that need a model download (semantic search, face and plate recognition, bird classification) therefore do not work.
- **Storage budget and retention.** `frigate-media` asks for 100 GiB; the seeded retention keeps no continuous video, motion 7 days, alerts and detections 14 days, snapshots 14 days. If the disk runs low anyway, Frigate deletes the oldest recordings once less than about an hour of recording space is left (configuration/record.md).
- **Config.** An init container copies the seed config to `/config/config.yml` only when there is none; after that the owner changes everything in Frigate's own Settings and the seed never overwrites it.
- **Detection** runs on the CPU with OpenVINO, upstream's default for a new install. On a box with an NVIDIA card that reports at least 1 GiB of memory (a OneMind threshold: decoding needs far less than a language model), the gateway renders `manifests-gpu/`: the same image with the `nvidia` RuntimeClass, one GPU and ffmpeg's `preset-nvidia` decoder seeded. Detection stays on the CPU there too.
- **Root, with four capabilities.** The image starts s6-overlay as root and has no non-root mode. Run as UID 1000 it stops at once ("/run belongs to uid 0"); as root with every capability dropped, s6 cannot hand its log folders to its log user and the log service fails. It runs with exactly `CHOWN`, `FOWNER`, `SETGID` and `SETUID` added, no privilege escalation, not privileged, RuntimeDefault seccomp. Each case was checked by running the pinned image with Docker on Linux (2026-11-22); with those four the UI answers 200 on 8971 and the API 200 on 5000.
- `/dev/shm` (512 MiB) and `/tmp/cache` (1 GiB) are memory volumes, as upstream's `shm_size` and tmpfs; they count against the 4 GiB memory limit.
- Probes run upstream's own health check (`curl http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/version` inside the container).

## First run

Source: [docs.frigate.video](https://docs.frigate.video) (configuration/authentication.md, "Onboarding"; guides/getting_started).

1. Install Frigate NVR from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-frigate`.
2. Read the first admin password: Frigate creates the user `admin` with a random password on its first start and prints it once in its log (owners: `GET /v1/apps/frigate/logs`). Sign in on port 8971 and set a new password under Settings > Users.
3. Add a camera with the camera wizard (Settings > Cameras) using its RTSP address.

## Not done yet

- **The install sandbox refuses it until a reviewed row exists.** The gateway runs every app namespace at Pod Security `restricted` unless `sdk/policy/app-objects.yaml` lists the app under `pod_security.reviewed` with a reason. Frigate needs `level: baseline` and `add_capabilities: [CHOWN, FOWNER, SETGID, SETUID]`; that change is a security review of its own (the file says so) and is not in this folder. `sdk/tools/tests/test_frigate_app.py` proves the sandbox accepts the app with exactly that row and refuses nothing else.
- **Cameras on the LAN are not reachable yet.** The gateway's default egress for a Market app is the internet minus the LAN (`network.default_egress` in `sdk/policy/app-objects.yaml`), and the app schema has no field to ask for LAN-only egress instead (the sandbox reads `spec.network.egress`, the schema does not accept it). Until it does, Frigate cannot pull RTSP from a LAN camera, and its internet egress is closed only by its own config.
- **No Coral or Intel/AMD GPU.** A USB Coral needs USB device access and Intel/AMD decoding needs `/dev/dri`; the contract allows no device access yet (validate-apps check 8; TAXONOMY lists `coral` under the proposed `spec.placement.devices`).
- No RTSP restream (8554) or WebRTC (8555), so no two-way audio; live view uses MSE/HLS over 8971.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: s6-overlay writes under `/run` and nginx renders its config at start.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices where upstream gives none.
- `metadata.tier` follows what `sdk/tools/app-gate` computes; `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4 check 4) sets tier **blocked** when an image has a CRITICAL vulnerability with a fix available. Trivy 0.76.2, run the way the gate runs it (remote image, `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, scanners `vuln,secret`) on 2026-11-22 against the pinned `0.18.3` digest, found 41 CRITICAL findings (one per CVE, package and version across both archs), 33 of them with a fix, 710 HIGH and no secrets. The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened.

- Fixable CRITICAL, by package: `curl` and `libcurl4` (CVE-2023-38545); `libexpat1` (CVE-2024-45491, CVE-2024-45492); the Mesa drivers `libgl1-mesa-dri`, `libglapi-mesa`, `libglx-mesa0`, `mesa-va-drivers`, `mesa-vulkan-drivers` (CVE-2026-40393); `libglib2.0-0` (CVE-2025-14087); `libgnutls30` (CVE-2026-33845, CVE-2026-42010); Kerberos `libgssapi-krb5-2`, `libk5crypto3`, `libkrb5-3`, `libkrb5support0` (CVE-2024-37371); `liblzma5` (CVE-2024-3094); `libpcre2-8-0` (CVE-2025-58050); `libsqlite3-0` (CVE-2025-3277); `libssl3` and `openssl` (CVE-2026-31789); `libxml2` (CVE-2024-56171); `perl-base` (CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-42496, CVE-2026-8376); `wget` (CVE-2024-38428); Go `stdlib` in a bundled binary (CVE-2022-23806, CVE-2023-24538, CVE-2023-24540, CVE-2024-24790, CVE-2025-68121).
- CRITICAL without a fix (recorded, not counted by the gate): `libglib2.0-0` CVE-2026-58016, `libsqlite3-0` CVE-2025-7458, `libxml2` CVE-2026-6653, `zlib1g` CVE-2023-45853, `libaom3` CVE-2023-6879, `libmbedcrypto7` CVE-2025-47917, CVE-2026-34873, CVE-2026-34875.

These are scanner results, not independently checked against each upstream advisory (UNVERIFIED per finding; for example the `liblzma5` match may be a version-range false positive). `0.18.3` is upstream's latest release (2026-11-19), so no fixed tag exists to move to.

To unblock: move the pin to an upstream Frigate release whose image fixes these findings (a tag that exists, read with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag, and the tier is never lifted by hand. Issue #245 stays open until the app installs.
